prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks based on the magic-wavelength principle, bringing neutral-atom timekeeping to unprecedented accuracy and stability

statement.case_for: After reading the other ballots I move B012 from my fifth place to the top of my configuration. It is the one candidate that seven of eight members rank, and I want to separate that breadth from merit: what persuades me is that the criteria I apply are met on the record. It is an invention (the magic-wavelength optical lattice, proposed by Katori around 2001-2003 and first demonstrated with strontium), it is original, and it has been experimentally verified many times over by independent clock comparisons at the 1e-18 level. It also opens a door to things people could not previously measure, such as the gravitational redshift across millimetres, tests of constant variation, and relativistic geodesy. The attribution is cleaner than in almost any other candidate on this list: one person conceived the scheme, and Ye's group, with its many-body clock work, took it to the performance frontier. Two laureates is a fair and defensible configuration.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that Hall and Haensch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already cover the comb and ion-control lineage, so a reader may see this as a continuation of metrology prizes. Credit for early experimental demonstrations also reaches beyond the two names: Takamoto and Katori's first strontium clock, Lemonde's group, and the Ludlow, Hinkley and Boyd teams at JILA, and I cannot settle exact priority dates from memory. Finally, the redefinition of the second has not yet happened. That is not a prize criterion, but some colleagues may prefer to wait for it. I do not think any of these defeats the case, but the citation must be written narrowly around the lattice-clock concept and its realization.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B012 first as a textbook measurement method that opens new observations, with Katori's concept and Ye's record performance as a clean two-person pairing.
responses.response: I agree with the core of this, and it is why I have moved up from fifth. I would qualify one thing. The 1e-18 figures and the millimetre redshift measurement are Ye's results, so they speak to the realization half of the citation, not to Katori's priority. The claim of originality rests on the 2001-2003 proposal and the first strontium demonstrations. I think we should state that distinction in the citation rather than let performance records carry the whole credit.

responses.point: Mehlig puts B057 first because Z2 topological order and the HgTe edge-channel experiment pair a clear mechanism with a measured conductance, while acknowledging that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited.
responses.response: I share your regard for theory-plus-experiment pairs, and I placed B057 sixth for the same reason you flag as a gap. The HgTe realization was proposed by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the experiment was done by Molenkamp's group, so a Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio leaves the link between prediction and observation without credit. I cannot be absolutely sure we would credit the right people. Four named contributors compete for three places, and the 2016 topological prize adds a risk of overlap. B012 has no comparable hole in the names, which is why it comes first for me.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube first as an instrument-driven opening of a new observational window, evidence for sources included, and notes that three names under-represent a collaboration of several hundred.
responses.response: I respect the instrument argument, and I put IceCube seventh, not lower, for that reason. The diffuse flux is a robust discovery. My concern is the standard I apply, that we are absolutely sure we have identified the people who did the original work. Here the work was done by a collaboration and by the Baikal and AMANDA predecessors, and you yourself note that the diffuse flux, the 2017-18 blazar and the NGC 1068 result point to different people. For source association I also want more than the current evidence. Until we agree which discovery is being rewarded, I find B012 easier to defend.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene first because a theoretical prediction was confirmed in a tunable platform, and also ranks MgO tunnel magnetoresistance third on the theory-to-measurement link.
responses.response: I have both candidates in my top three and they are my two alternatives. For B036 my reservation is the unsettled pairing mechanism and the allocation among Bistritzer, MacDonald and the experimental team, including graduate-student contributions and Dean's group. The experiment of Jarillo-Herrero's group is the original observation, though, so I would not dismiss it. On B005 we differ on the theory share. I would credit Parkin and Yuasa for the two 2004 experiments and consider Butler's prediction a separate matter, since Mathon and Umerski made the same prediction independently. Neither alternative, in my view, is as well settled on attribution as the lattice clock.

uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley and ion-clock groups when worded credit is narrowed to Katori and Ye, and whether priority claims for early strontium demonstrations hold up against the record.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second, and whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes make a metrology award look repetitive.
For B036 and B005, whether the theory share (Bistritzer versus MacDonald; Butler versus Mathon and Umerski) can be assigned with the certainty I want.
statement.conflict_note: My first-ranked opening candidate, B021 (aberration-corrected electron optics), is in my own field of electron microscopy, so I should not drive that discussion. I am also a Fellow of the University of Tokyo (since 2025) with long-running exchanges there, and Katori's affiliation with that university, as far as I recall, is a connection colleagues may wish to weigh when considering B012, though it involves no collaboration with him that the provided profile shows. No other specific conflict is apparent from the profile.
